signals.summary: 'Slow travel' is the dominant framing this cycle — unhurried stays on farms, islands and river boats, sold on atmosphere and landscape rather than itinerary.
signals.why_now: The Guardian on Slovenia's 'secret valley' slow-travel story (~7h), a 200-year-old working-farm retreat in Portugal (~42h), 'Slow Travel through Setouchi' Japan (~43h) and Design Milk's reimagined Nile dahabeah (~65h) — five independent slow-travel pieces inside three days.

signals.summary: A cluster of new and expanding European rail routes — night trains and high-speed links — is driving a rail-travel wave framed around scenery and slow overland journeys.
signals.why_now: 'Europe by Night: New Train to Copenhagen and Malmo' (~29h), 'Four of Europe's coolest cities set to be connected by a new sleeper train' (~52h) and 'high-speed trains London to Europe every 15 minutes' (~51h) — four independent rail pieces in two days.

signals.summary: Curiosity-led travel to unusual, overlooked places — lighthouses, unusual picnic spots, quiet towns — carries strongly, all rendering as striking place-and-object stills.
signals.why_now: Atlas Obscura's stream of unusual places this cycle (unusual picnic spots ~17h, Cape Bear Lighthouse ~17h, recycled-material sculptures ~72h) plus a 'best hidden-gem destinations' roundup (~50h); leans on one curatorial outlet, so corroboration is moderate.
